'''Kialo''' is an online structured debate platform with [[argument map]]s in the form of debate trees. It is a collaborative reasoning tool for thoughtful discussion, understanding different points of view, and [[collaborative decision-making]], showing [[argument]]s for and against claims underneath user-submitted theses or questions.<ref name="chonicEd"/><ref name="fitimes"/><ref name="about">{{cite web |title=About |url=https://www.kialo.com/about |website=Kialo |access-date=9 June 2023 |language=en |archive-date=7 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230607192456/https://www.kialo.com/about |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="10.1145/3485447.3512144">{{cite book |last1=Agarwal |first1=Vibhor |last2=Joglekar |first2=Sagar |last3=Young |first3=Anthony P. |last4=Sastry |first4=Nishanth |title=Proceedings of the ACM Web Conference 2022 |chapter=GraphNLI: A Graph-based Natural Language Inference Model for Polarity Prediction in Online Debates |date=25 April 2022 |pages=2729–2737 |doi=10.1145/3485447.3512144|arxiv=2202.08175 |isbn=9781450390965 |s2cid=246867079 }}</ref>

[[File:Structured online debate – Kialo debate tree.png|thumb|Kialo debate tree schema with {{tooltip|an example path through it|all Con-argument boxes and some Pros were emptied to illustrate an example path}}.<ref name="Bolton"/>]]
[[File:Collective determinination of argument impact.png|thumb|Example partial argument tree with claims and corresponding impact votes for arguments within the given line of reasoning, one form of {{vanchor|collective determination of argument weights}} that is used on the platform<ref name="impactrating">{{cite book |last1=Durmus |first1=Esin |last2=Ladhak |first2=Faisal |last3=Cardie |first3=Claire |title=Proceedings of the 2019 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing and the 9th International Joint Conference on Natural Language Processing (EMNLP-IJCNLP) |chapter=The Role of Pragmatic and Discourse Context in Determining Argument Impact |pages=5667–5677 |doi=10.18653/v1/D19-1568 |date=2019|arxiv=2004.03034 |s2cid=202768765 }}</ref>]]

The deliberative discourse platform is designed to present hundreds of supporting or opposing arguments in a dynamic argument [[tree structure|tree]]<ref>{{cite book |title=Development Co-operation Report 2021 Shaping a Just Digital Transformation: Shaping a Just Digital Transformation |date=21 December 2021 |publisher=OECD Publishing |isbn=978-92-64-85686-8 |page=327 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ARtZEAAAQBAJ |language=en |access-date=11 June 2023 |archive-date=11 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611175141/https://books.google.com/books?id=ARtZEAAAQBAJ |url-status=live }}</ref> and is streamlined for [[rational]] civil debate on topics such as [[philosophy|philosophical]] questions, policy deliberations, entertainment, ethics, science questions, and [[Lists of unsolved problems|unsolved problems]] or subjects of disagreement in general.<ref name="fitimes"/><ref name="chonicEd"/><ref name="makeuseofKialo"/><ref name="Skitalinskaya"/>

Argument-boxes are structured into hierarchical branches where the root is the main thesis (or theses) of the debate, enabling [[deliberation]] and navigable [[debate]]s between opposing perspectives. A debate is divided into Pro (supporting) and Con (refuting or devaluing) columns where registered users can add arguments and [[voting system|rate]] the {{tooltip|impact on the weight or validity|how large it affects the strength of the claim it addresses}} of the parent claim. The arguments {{tooltip|are sorted according to the rating average|the average rating is shown at the top of the argument box and as of 2023 is based on equal-impact headcounts of registered voters}}.{{refn|name=impactRatings|<ref name="fitimes"/><ref name="makeuseofKialo">{{cite web |title=5 Best Debate Sites to Civilly and Logically Argue Online About Opinions |url=https://www.makeuseof.com/best-debate-sites/ |website=MUO |access-date=9 June 2023 |language=en |date=14 May 2022 |archive-date=11 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611174156/https://www.makeuseof.com/best-debate-sites/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="techlearning"/><ref name="10.1145/3485447.3512144"/><ref name="Allaire">{{cite book |last1=Allaire |first1=Franklin S. |last2=Killham |first2=Jennifer E. |title=Teaching and Learning Online: Science for Elementary Grade Levels |date=1 April 2022 |publisher=IAP |isbn=978-1-64802-876-2 |page=105 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=kpBwEAAAQBAJ |language=en |access-date=11 June 2023 |archive-date=11 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611175133/https://books.google.com/books?id=kpBwEAAAQBAJ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Liu">{{cite arXiv |title=Exploring Discourse Structures for Argument Impact Classification |eprint=2106.00976 |last1=Liu |first1=Xin |last2=Ou |first2=Jiefu |last3=Song |first3=Yangqiu |last4=Jiang |first4=Xin |year=2021 |class=cs.CL }}</ref><ref name="guo"/>}}

Its argument tree structure enables detailed scrutiny of claims at all levels of the tree<ref name="structured"/> and allows users to for example quickly understand why a decision was made or which of the aggregated arguments swayed it this way.<ref name="fitimes"/> Newcomers can join a debate at any time and look back at the structured discussion history, and then weigh in at the right place with their new argument or their comment on a specific argument.<ref name="chonicEd"/><ref name="techlearning"/><ref name="Mahoney"/> The design presets a structure on debates "that allows participants to easily see, process, and ultimately assess the many facets of competing claims".<ref name="structured"/>

The word Kialo is [[Esperanto]] for "reason".<ref name="fitimes">{{cite news |last1=Margolis |first1=Jonathan |title=Meet the start-up that wants to sell you civilised debate |url=https://www.ft.com/content/4c19005c-ff5f-11e7-9e12-af73e8db3c71 |access-date=9 June 2023 |work=[[Financial Times]] |date=24 January 2018 |archive-date=11 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611174157/https://www.ft.com/content/4c19005c-ff5f-11e7-9e12-af73e8db3c71 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="chonicEd"/> The platform is the world's largest argument mapping and structured debate site.<ref name="fakenews">{{cite journal |last1=Ovidiu |first1=Acomi |last2=Nicoleta |first2=Acomi |last3=Roxana |first3=Andrei Elena |last4=Francesca |first4=Dadomo |last5=Domitille |first5=Hocq |last6=Luis |first6=Ochoa Siguencia |last7=Renata |first7=Ochoa-Daderska |last8=Fabiola |first8=Porcelli |last9=Savino |first9=Ricchiuto |last10=Ana |first10=Velasco Garcia |title=Empowering Youth to Critically Analyse Fake News. Strategies of Intervention and Good Practices. |doi=10.5281/zenodo.6549573 |url=https://doi.org/10.5281%2Fzenodo.6549573 |date=15 May 2022 |access-date=11 June 2023 |archive-date=21 July 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230721233306/https://zenodo.org/record/6549573 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="10.1145/3461564.3461584"/>

== Overview ==
Users can comment on every Pro or Con, for example for requesting sources or expansions.<ref name="makeuseofKialo"/> Recent activities of a debate are shown in a panel on the right side of the respective debate.<ref name="makeuseofKialo"/> Debates can be found through the search or on the Explore page through their descriptions and topic-[[Tag (metadata)|tags]].<ref name="10.1145/3485447.3512144"/>

Mere comments that do not make a constructive point (a self-contained argument backed by reasoning) are not allowed and are picked up by other users and moderators.<ref name="fitimes"/><ref name="10.1145/3485447.3512144"/><ref name="graphbased"/> "Civil language and sensible observations from opposing perspectives" can be seen also in debates about controversial topics.<ref name="irishdebate"/> The site by-design incentivizes fair, rigorous, open-minded dialogue.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Alfano |first1=Mark |last2=Klein |first2=Colin |last3=Ridder |first3=Jeroen de |title=Social Virtue Epistemology |date=29 July 2022 |publisher=Taylor & Francis |isbn=978-1-000-60730-7 |page=43 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=L1J-EAAAQBAJ |language=en |access-date=11 June 2023 |archive-date=11 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611175136/https://books.google.com/books?id=L1J-EAAAQBAJ |url-status=live }}</ref> Contributors making claims often also write counterpoints to their own contribution.<ref name="fitimes"/> Claims need to be shorter than 500 characters and can link to external sources.<ref name="niemanreports"/>

Debate trees can also start off with multiple theses – such as {{tooltip|different policy options|these can be precluding or different aspects that can be complementary; the example here is "what kind of restrictions should be placed on solar geoengineering research, if it were to happen" which has multiple non-precluding these delineated by stakeholder, corresponding to "research conducted by the government, universities, and private sector respectively"}} or hypotheses. Claims can link to related debates or include segments of them.<ref name="harvardexample"/> In the discussion tab of each claim, users can make edit proposals (e.g. for accuracy, improving sources, or changing scope), decide if the argument should be moved or copied to another branch, call for archiving a claim, and ask for extra evidence or clarification.<ref name="resourceAndDiscussion"/>

Debates can grow large and complex for which a [[sunburst diagram]] {{tooltip|visualization of the topology of the debate|the visualization is shown at the top of any debate – in it the central node is the core thesis and subsequent levels of arguments radiate out from the central thesis}}<ref name="10.1145/3485447.3512144"/><ref name="tudelft">{{cite web |title=Developing critical thinking skills with Kialo – Library Trends |url=https://trends.tudl.tudelft.nl/2018/01/16/developing-critical-thinking-skills-with-kialo/ |publisher=TU Delft |access-date=9 June 2023 |date=16 January 2018 |archive-date=11 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611174156/https://trends.tudl.tudelft.nl/2018/01/16/developing-critical-thinking-skills-with-kialo/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="structured"/><ref name="infographic"/><ref name="10.1145/3469595.3469615">{{cite book |last1=Anastasiou |first1=Lucas |last2=De Liddo |first2=Anna |title=Extended Abstracts of the 2021 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems |chapter=Making Sense of Online Discussions: Can Automated Reports help? |date=8 May 2021 |pages=1–7 |doi=10.1145/3411763.3451815 |publisher=Association for Computing Machinery|isbn=9781450380959 |s2cid=233987842 }}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Kiesel |first1=Johannes |last2=Spina |first2=Damiano |last3=Wachsmuth |first3=Henning |last4=Stein |first4=Benno |title=CUI 2021 - 3rd Conference on Conversational User Interfaces |chapter=The Meant, the Said, and the Understood: Conversational Argument Search and Cognitive Biases |date=27 July 2021 |pages=1–5 |doi=10.1145/3469595.3469615 |publisher=Association for Computing Machinery|isbn=9781450389983 |s2cid=236203094 }}</ref> and the search functionality can be useful. Each debate also has a chat-box.<ref>{{cite journal |title=A Blended Approach to Flipped Learning for Teaching Debate – Using Kialo Edu for EFL Debate Preparation|first1=Heather |last1=Woodward|first2=Laura|last2=Padfield|journal=Journal of Multilingual Pedagogy and Practice |year=2021 |volume=1 |doi=10.14992/00020487}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Taking it to Task Volume 5, Issue 1, Summer 2021 |url=https://www.tblsig.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/2021-Summer-Taking-it-to-Task.pdf |access-date=10 June 2023 |archive-date=11 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611174157/https://www.tblsig.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/2021-Summer-Taking-it-to-Task.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref> In cases where e.g. a "Con" is a point against multiple in the "Pros", users – through moderators – can link these arguments at the respective places to avoid duplication of content and allowing a clean chain for people to understand which points are arguments against each other.<ref name="makeuseofKialo"/> Contributions of users are tracked, enabling a board of thought-leaders for every debate.<ref name="infographic">{{cite web |title=Statistics and the Infographic {{!}} Kialo Edu Help Center |url=https://support.kialo-edu.com/en/hc/statistics-and-the-infographic/ |website=support.kialo-edu.com |access-date=10 June 2023 |date=5 August 2022 |archive-date=11 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611174157/https://support.kialo-edu.com/en/hc/statistics-and-the-infographic/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Other [[gamification]] elements include a feature to thank users for their contributions.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Feger |first1=Marc |title=Online argumentation and social media: What they can learn from each other |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/352441941 |access-date=11 June 2023 |date=May 2021}}</ref><ref name="niemanreports"/>

The "[[Point of view (philosophy)|Perspectives]]" feature allows users to see 'Impact' ratings of supporters and opposers of a thesis as well as of the debate's moderators and individual contributors.<ref name="10.31219/osf.io/cdfq7"/> It thereby enables participants to see a debate from other participants' perspectives and to sort by them.<ref name="10.31219/osf.io/cdfq7"/> In [[#Kialo Edu|Kialo Edu]], this feature lets teachers view votes for a whole class, individuals, or supporters/opponents of a specific thesis.<ref>{{cite web |title=Teaching students to take different perspectives with Kialo Edu |url=https://blog.kialo-edu.com/tips-and-tricks/teaching-students-to-take-different-perspectives-on-kialo-edu/ |access-date=9 June 2023 |date=17 May 2023 |archive-date=11 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611174159/https://blog.kialo-edu.com/tips-and-tricks/teaching-students-to-take-different-perspectives-on-kialo-edu/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Users in both versions of Kialo can vote on the overall debate topic as well as on individual claims to express their perspectives or conclusions, with the [[Explanation|rationale]] (i.e. the main causal arguments) why they voted on the veracity of the thesis as they did not being captured.<ref name="Dialectics"/> Voting can be done by any registered user while navigating through any debate that has voting enabled or via using the Guided Voting [[Wizard (software)|wizard]] user interface that automatically walks through branches.<ref>{{cite web |title=Guided Voting {{!}} Kialo Help Center |url=https://support.kialo.com/en/hc/guided-voting/ |website=support.kialo.com |date=6 April 2023 |access-date=18 July 2023 |archive-date=4 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230604164528/https://support.kialo.com/en/hc/guided-voting/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

As of 2021, Kialo doesn't have a mobile app.<ref name="ubckialo">{{cite web |title=Debating the Issues with Kialo {{!}} ETEC523: Mobile and Open Learning |url=https://blogs.ubc.ca/etec523/2021/02/07/debating-the-issues-with-kialo/ |website=blogs.ubc.ca |publisher=[[University of British Columbia]] |access-date=9 June 2023 |archive-date=11 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611174156/https://blogs.ubc.ca/etec523/2021/02/07/debating-the-issues-with-kialo/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Contents ==
[[File:Number of claim revision pairs in each debate category of Kialo.png|thumb|Diagram roughly showing the shares of site content per top debate category; each argument can be [[version control software|revised]] and the diagram shows the numbers of revisions in each category which {{tooltip|roughly reflect which categories are most actively and/or extensively debated|this does not show the number of debates or arguments per category; it only shows the 20 most frequent categories; in some cases arguments may get revised disproportionally such as due to a higher share of inexperienced users making many mistakes including typos.}}.<ref name="Skitalinskaya"/>]]
A 2018 report stated the collaborative argument platform hosts more than 10,000 debates in various languages.<ref name="niemanreports"/> It also hosts private debates. The website claims that it has over 18,000 public debates as of July 2023, as well as over 1 million votes and over 720,000 claims.<ref>{{cite web |title=Explore Popular Debates, Discussions and Critical Thinking… |url=https://www.kialo.com/ |website=Kialo |access-date=16 July 2023 |language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230718113255/https://www.kialo.com/|archive-date=18 July 2023}}</ref> Debates can be found via the site's internal search and up to six tags per debate.

[[Preprint]] studies have scraped public debates on over 1.4K issues with over 130K statements as of October 2019<ref name="Detecting"/> and 1628 debates, related to over 1120 categories, with 124,312 unique claims as of June 26, 2020.<ref name="Skitalinskaya"/>

== Kialo Inc. ==
The site is run by Kialo Inc. It was founded by German-born entrepreneur and [[London School of Economics and Political Science]] graduate Errikos Pitsos in August 2017 and is based in [[Brooklyn]] and Berlin.<ref name="fitimes"/><ref name="chonicEd"/> According to a 2018 report, the site does not show advertisements and does not sell user's data.<!--The report stated that Kialo is self-funded and that at the time it had 50 employees.--><ref name="fitimes"/> The for-profit company was founded in 2011,<ref>{{cite web |title=Kialo - Products, Competitors, Financials, Employees, Headquarters Locations |url=https://www.cbinsights.com/company/kialo |website=CB Insights |access-date=9 June 2023 |archive-date=11 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611174156/https://www.cbinsights.com/company/kialo |url-status=live }}</ref>{{additional citation needed|date=June 2023}} Pitsos began to develop the concept in 2012<ref name="niemanreports">{{cite web |title=Four News Startups Trying To Improve Civic Discourse |url=https://niemanreports.org/articles/four-news-startups-trying-to-improve-civic-discourse/ |website=Nieman Reports |date=27 June 2018 |access-date=11 June 2023 |archive-date=11 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611174205/https://niemanreports.org/articles/four-news-startups-trying-to-improve-civic-discourse/ |url-status=live }}</ref> and described various specifics of the system in 2014.<ref>{{cite web |title=US Patent Application for Management, Evaluation And Visualization Method, System And User Interface For Discussions And Assertions Patent Application (Application #20150220580 issued August 6, 2015) - Justia Patents Search |url=https://patents.justia.com/patent/20150220580 |website=patents.justia.com |access-date=9 June 2023 |archive-date=11 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611174155/https://patents.justia.com/patent/20150220580 |url-status=live }}</ref> In 2018, he stated that they intend to make money by selling the platform to companies as a deliberation and decision-making tool.<ref name="niemanreports"/> The site is free to use for the public and in education.<ref name="techlearning"/> According to the site, as of 2023 Kialo.com is a non-revenue generating site with no ads and no reselling of user data.<ref name="terms">{{cite web |title=Terms of Service {{!}} Kialo |url=https://www.kialo.com/terms |website=www.kialo.com |access-date=18 July 2023 |archive-date=2 July 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230702114845/https://www.kialo.com/terms |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Applications and adoption ==
=== Adopted applications ===
{{See also|Education#Development}}
Applications of its content or the platform in society include:
* Teachers and professors, especially in high schools – including the universities Harvard and Princeton, are using Kialo for class discussions and exercises in critical thinking and reasoning,<ref name="fitimes"/><ref name="ubckialo"/><ref name="niemanreports"/><ref name="Mahoney">{{cite web |last1=Mahoney |first1=Jon |title=Drawing the Line: Integrating Kialo to Deepen Critical Thinking in Debate |url=https://rikkyo.repo.nii.ac.jp/?action=repository_action_common_download&item_id=22525&item_no=1&attribute_id=22&file_no=1 |access-date=2023-06-11 |archive-date=2023-06-11 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611174156/https://rikkyo.repo.nii.ac.jp/?action=repository_action_common_download&item_id=22525&item_no=1&attribute_id=22&file_no=1 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="fakenews"/><ref name="Dialectics"/> as consolidating understanding of materials covered in recent classes,<ref name="fakenews"/> more useful and engaging learning experiences,<ref education during lockdown period of COVID-19 pandemic |journal=International Journal of Educational Research Open |date=2020 |volume=1 |article-number=100012 |doi=10.1016/j.ijedro.2020.100012 |doi-access=free|pmid=35059663 |pmc=7832355 }}</ref> for clearing up [[List of common misconceptions|misconceptions]],<ref name="Allaire"/> teaching logical fallacies and rational argumentation,<ref>{{cite book |last1=Wasson |first1=Barbara |last2=Zörgő |first2=Szilvia |title=Advances in Quantitative Ethnography: Third International Conference, ICQE 2021, Virtual Event, November 6–11, 2021, Proceedings |date=11 January 2022 |publisher=Springer Nature |isbn=978-3-030-93859-8 |page=34 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=wdFYEAAAQBAJ |language=en |access-date=11 June 2023 |archive-date=11 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611175136/https://books.google.com/books?id=wdFYEAAAQBAJ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="digimedi"/> for academic |isbn=978-1-000-24635-3 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=rYH4DwAAQBAJ |language=en |chapter=Demonstrating Learning in the Remote Classroom |access-date=11 June 2023 |archive-date=11 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611175136/https://books.google.com/books?id=6NGZEAAAQBAJ |url-status=live }}</ref> Like for debaters of the main site, access for schools and universities is free. '''{{vanchor|Kialo Edu}}''' is the custom version of Kialo specifically designed for classroom use where debates are private and locked to invited students.<ref name="978-1-0718-8702-8">{{cite book |last1=Mills |first1=Afrika Afeni |title=Open Windows, Open Minds: Developing Antiracist, Pro-Human Students |date=16 June 2022 |publisher=Corwin Press |isbn=978-1-0718-8702-8 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=cL9pEAAAQBAJ&pg=PT231 |language=en |access-date=11 June 2023 |archive-date=11 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611175140/https://books.google.com/books?id=cL9pEAAAQBAJ&pg=PT231 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="techlearning">{{cite web |last1=Edwards |first1=Luke |title=What is Kialo? Best Tips and Tricks |url=https://www.techlearning.com/how-to/what-is-kialo-best-tips-and-tricks |website=TechLearningMagazine |access-date=9 June 2023 |language=en |date=7 July 2021 |archive-date=11 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611174155/https://www.techlearning.com/how-to/what-is-kialo-best-tips-and-tricks |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Butcher |first1=Charity |title=Creating Online Debates Using Kialo Edu |url=https://educate.apsanet.org/wp-content/uploads/Creating-Online-Debates-Using-Kialo-Edu.pdf |website= |access-date=9 June 2023 |archive-date=11 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611174159/https://educate.apsanet.org/wp-content/uploads/Creating-Online-Debates-Using-Kialo-Edu.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Lang-Raad |first1=Nathan D. |title=Never Stop Asking: Teaching Students to be Better Critical Thinkers |date=18 April 2023 |publisher=John Wiley & Sons |isbn=978-1-119-88754-6 |page=114 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=-7OvEAAAQBAJ |language=en |access-date=11 June 2023 |archive-date=11 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611175138/https://books.google.com/books?id=-7OvEAAAQBAJ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="fakenews"/><ref>{{cite web |title=Try Out a Kialo Classroom Debate for High School {{!}} Kialo Edu Help Center |url=https://support.kialo-edu.com/en/hc/try-out-a-kialo-classroom-debate-for-high-school/ |website=support.kialo-edu.com |access-date=9 June 2023 |date=5 August 2022 |archive-date=11 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611174155/https://support.kialo-edu.com/en/hc/try-out-a-kialo-classroom-debate-for-high-school/ |url-status=live }}</ref>
**Kialo allows teachers to provide feedback to students on their ideas, argument structure, and research quality while it is left to other students to rate the impacts of their peers' arguments.<ref name="techlearning"/>
**Students can be allowed to contribute anonymously which may be useful for controversial issues as well as for safeguarding [[privacy in education]].<ref>{{cite web |title=How students can benefit from Anonymous Discussions |url=https://blog.kialo-edu.com/teaching-strategies/how-students-benefit-from-anonymous-discussions/ |access-date=9 June 2023 |date=8 May 2023 |archive-date=11 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611174155/https://blog.kialo-edu.com/teaching-strategies/how-students-benefit-from-anonymous-discussions/ |url-status=live }}</ref>
**Students are or can be encouraged to back up their claims with evidence which can foster [[digital literacy]] and research skills.<ref name="techlearning"/>
**Students and teachers can use it to arrange their thoughts when structuring an essay or project.<ref name="techlearning"/>
* The site's name was decided on internally using the software.<ref name="chonicEd"/>

=== Prototypical and theoretical applications ===
{{See also|Evidence-based policy|Research question#ICTs, participation and routine procedures}}
[[File:Intelligent assistant for argumentative support and arguments inquiry.png|thumb|Structured debates from the site could be used for intelligent assistants and similar AI software<ref name="10.1145/3469595.3469615"/> such as in computational reasoning; such bots have been called "artificial deliberative agents" (ADAs).<ref name="Betz">{{cite journal |last1=Betz |first1=Gregor |title=Natural-Language Multi-Agent Simulations of Argumentative Opinion Dynamics |journal=Journal of Artificial Societies and Social Simulation |article-number=2 |doi=10.18564/jasss.4725 |date=2022|volume=25 |arxiv=2104.06737 |s2cid=233231231 }}</ref>]]
[[File:Basic design of artificial deliberative agents (ADAs) for argumentation.png|thumb|Example of an ADA contributing missing information to a debate via crawled Kialo data and selected based [[natural language processing|on the prior conversation]] and crawled [[#collective determination of argument weights|argument weight ratings]]<ref name="Betz"/>]]
Potential, theoretical, prototypical or little-used applications include:
;Education
* Improving critical thinking skills of society at large as well as facilitating deep or [[Neuroenhancement#Conventional methods and foundational strategies|efficient thinking and deepening research and debates]]{{Broken anchor|date=2024-06-06|bot=User:Cewbot/log/20201008/configuration|target_link=Neuroenhancement#Conventional methods and foundational strategies|reason= The anchor (Conventional methods and foundational strategies) [[Special:Diff/1193040114|has been deleted]].}}<ref name="chonicEd"/><ref name="tudelft"/><ref name="techlearning"/><ref name="Mahoney"/> where e.g. discussions are less shallow<ref name="structured"/> and the well-known or many arguments have already been made and in many cases aren't unreasonably over- or underrated.
** Pitsos claimed that "we're training students to be very good test-takers instead of critical thinkers", suggesting teaching people to think things through may be more important or neglected compared to essay writing skills.<ref name="chonicEd"/>
* Many young people and adults are "submerged into a sea of dispersed information", "[b]rowsing and engaging in superficial thinking activities". Kialo could counteract this issue and help people develop good sane reasoning.<ref name="tudelft"/>

;Academia, [[research and development|R&D]] and [[policy]]
* Three scholars from three prestigious U.S. universities outlined possible benefits in this domain, including applications beyond higher education such as for [[scholarly communication|academic communication]]. They suggest the debate platform could be used for structuring the communication of open [[peer-review]] by helping those giving feedback to "hone in on[sic] core arguments and pieces of evidence in an even more direct way" than annotated commenting.<ref name="tudelft"/><ref name="structured">{{cite web |last1=Chaudoin |first1=Stephen |last2=Shapiro |first2=Jacob |last3=Tingley |first3=Dustin |title=Revolutionizing Teaching and Research with a Structured Debate Platform |url=https://scholar.harvard.edu/sites/scholar.harvard.edu/files/dtingley/files/structureddebate.pdf |website=scholar.harvard.edu |date=August 2017 |access-date=2023-06-11 |archive-date=2023-06-11 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611174154/https://scholar.harvard.edu/sites/scholar.harvard.edu/files/dtingley/files/structureddebate.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref>
* It could be used to evaluate [[natural language processing|extracted argument]] structures and sequences from raw texts,<ref name="structured"/> as in a [[Semantic Web]] for arguments. Such "[[argument mining]]", to which Kialo is the largest structured source so far, could e.g. be used to assess the completeness and effectiveness of an argumentative discussion<ref name="guo"/> or to augment it (with additional arguments, contextual information, assessments, refuting evidence or supporting data).<ref name="Bolton"/>
* A [[security studies]] paper suggested it could be used for "managing arguments more effectively than traditional paragraph/bullet-point approaches". It claims that "[[Complex system|complexity]] demands adaptation" but also notes that "Kialo's simplicity does pose some weaknesses and limitations, and in general current systems cannot reliably automate analysis or synthesis of arguments in the same way that statistical packages can automate analysis of data".<ref name="Complexity">{{cite journal |title=Complexity Demands Adaptation: Two Proposals for Facilitating Better Debate in International Relations and Conflict Research |journal=Georgetown Security Studies Review |date=30 November 2022 |url=https://georgetownsecuritystudiesreview.org/2022/11/30/complexity-demands-adaptation-two-proposals-for-facilitating-better-debate-in-international-relations-and-conflict-research/ |access-date=11 June 2023 |archive-date=11 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611174156/https://georgetownsecuritystudiesreview.org/2022/11/30/complexity-demands-adaptation-two-proposals-for-facilitating-better-debate-in-international-relations-and-conflict-research/ |url-status=live }}</ref>
* The site could be used by companies and government organizations as "intuitive debate software [[Participative decision-making in organizations|for internal discussions and decision-making]]".<ref name="fitimes"/><ref name="tudelft"/>
* It could aid in the [[policymaking|search for the best policies]] and course of action,<ref name="structured"/> including for '[[wicked problem]]s'<ref name="10.1145/3461564.3461584"/> and issues where there is a large [[Political polarization|polarization]]. This may include "experiments of [[deliberative democracy]] inside local governments".<ref name="niemanreports"/>
* With a platform like Kialo, users provide "both data on what they see is in the landscape of relevant arguments but also some indication of what they think is [[importance|important]] [or has [[prioritization|priority]]] in determining their policy preferences" and "also shows which arguments the individual did not find persuasive, and possibly which rebuttals to a particular argument [was] used to discard it."<ref name="structured"/> Current functionality of the site may still be insufficient for the latter outside of experiments.
* It could increase [[efficiency]] in [[knowledge acquisition]], including concerning [[information overload]] on social media.<ref name="guo"/>
* Policy-makers and scientists could use platforms and debates like these to engage with each other as well as the public<ref name="harvardexample"/> if they were aware of it and used it. Considering only argument trees beneath theses, its arguments-crowdsourcing and revision principles are not or less vulnerable to framing-issues, intentionally placed attackable segments, weak or missing arguments, [[straw man]] points, oversimplification, agenda-setting and other issues that may be common in contemporary public political debates.
* The debate trees can be used to identify arguments that are seen as most credible, as well as reveal which areas of argumentation lack support, precedent, or evidence,<ref name="structured"/> which may be useful for subsequent work or [[Metascience|more efficient and useful science]] (as in identifying little-supported assumptions, providing key missing data, or researching key [[Research question|open questions]]).

;General
* Writers in general, as well as possibly major other opinion leaders, could populate a Kialo debate with their arguments and release it alongside the traditional linear written format,<ref name="structured"/> albeit such would mean the arguments would be open to scrutiny, with such being more accessible than large and fans-dominated unstructured comment sections or may already be part of an existing debate tree. They could also use the site in other ways such as for selecting questions to pose to interviewees or for selecting unexplored questions to investigate and report on.
* It could be used for legal cases.<ref name="structured"/>
* Websites could embed read-only argument trees (or branches) from the site.<ref name="niemanreports"/>
* More broadly, the site's content could be used for reflective brainstorming, and as a [[crowdsourcing]] resource for points to use in other media (e.g. long-form text). It enables detailed exploration of some theses or topics as the visual reasoning through tree-based structure allows for many levels of depth and for follow-up questions in the discussion tab of each claim.{{refn|name=resourceAndDiscussion|<ref name="Mahoney"/><ref name="Dialectics">{{cite book |last1=Carroll |first1=John M. |last2=Sun |first2=Na |last3=Beck |first3=Jordan |title=Learning in a Digital World: Perspective on Interactive Technologies for Formal and Informal Education |date=2019 |publisher=Springer |isbn=978-981-13-8265-9 |pages=37–58 |chapter-url=https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-981-13-8265-9_3 |language=en |chapter=Creating Dialectics to Learn: Infrastructures, Practices, and Challenges |doi=10.1007/978-981-13-8265-9_3 |s2cid=195785108 |access-date=2023-06-11 |archive-date=2023-06-11 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611174155/https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-981-13-8265-9_3 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="10.1145/3461564.3461584">{{cite book |last1=De Liddo |first1=Anna |last2=Strube |first2=Rosa |title=C&T '21: Proceedings of the 10th International Conference on Communities & Technologies - Wicked Problems in the Age of Tech |chapter=Understanding Failures and Potentials of Argumentation Tools for Public Deliberation |date=21 June 2021 |pages=75–88 |doi=10.1145/3461564.3461584 |publisher=Association for Computing Machinery|isbn=9781450390569 |s2cid=235494842 }}</ref><ref name="Popescu">{{cite journal |last1=Popescu |first1=C. |last2=Cocarascu |first2=O. |last3=Toni |first3=F. |title=A platform for crowdsourcing corpora for argumentative |journal=The International Workshop on Dialogue, Explanation and Argumentation in Human-Agent Interaction (DEXAHAI) |date=15 December 2018 |hdl=10044/1/71110 |url=https://spiral.imperial.ac.uk/handle/10044/1/71110 |language=en-US-GB |access-date=11 June 2023 |archive-date=11 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611174200/https://spiral.imperial.ac.uk/handle/10044/1/71110 |url-status=live }}</ref>}} The founder stated that "The public debates are basically supposed to become a site where people can go and inform themselves. If a debate has over 2,000 unique arguments, it's going to be hard to find an argument that's not in there already. You can go there, similar to [[Wikipedia]], and read."<ref name="chonicEd"/>

=== Research ===<!--Use in research and as subject of research-->
[[File:Revision histories of argumentative claims from the online debate platform Kialo (collaborative refinement for optimal arguments).png|thumb|Claims can [[version control software|continuously be revised]] collaboratively; such changes are categorized by the user via a set of edit-types.<ref name="Revise"/><ref name="Durmus">{{cite book |last1=Durmus |first1=Esin |last2=Ladhak |first2=Faisal |last3=Cardie |first3=Claire |title=Proceedings of the 57th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics |chapter=Determining Relative Argument Specificity and Stance for Complex Argumentative Structures |pages=4630–4641 |doi=10.18653/v1/P19-1456 |date=2019|arxiv=1906.11313 |s2cid=195699602 }}</ref><ref name="Skitalinskaya">{{cite arXiv |title=Learning From Revisions: Quality Assessment of Claims in Argumentation at Scale |eprint=2101.10250 |last1=Skitalinskaya |first1=Gabriella |last2=Klaff |first2=Jonas |last3=Wachsmuth |first3=Henning |year=2021 |class=cs.CL }}</ref>]]
Kialo is a subject of research studies and its data has been used in research as there are datasets of its contents<ref name="10.1145/3485447.3512144"/><ref name="Liu"/><ref name="Revise"/><ref name="Skitalinskaya"/><ref name="impactrating"/> and the site allows exporting [[Comma-separated values|CSV]] files<ref name="structured"/> as well as [[Web crawling|crawling]] and filtering debates.<ref name="Bolton">{{cite arXiv |title=High Quality Real-Time Structured Debate Generation |eprint=2012.00209 |last1=Bolton |first1=Eric |last2=Calderwood |first2=Alex |last3=Christensen |first3=Niles |last4=Kafrouni |first4=Jerome |last5=Drori |first5=Iddo |year=2020 |class=cs.CL }}</ref><ref name="Betz"/>

;Content analysis in social science and belief studies
The contents can also be analyzed to e.g. show the most common Con rationale-types and factors in general,<ref name="Detecting"/> or reveal the most contested arguments where ratings <!--largest discrepancy-->diverge the most for a given topic.

The site's founder proposed the types of arguments and ways people reason could be investigated as well as the "performance of Kialo versus long-form text in [[Belief#Belief studies|making people change their minds]]".<ref name="chonicEd"/> One study suggests arguers seem to change their viewpoints more readily when a fact they believe has evidence and is undermined when compared to prior beliefs without {{tooltip|any specified supporting data|"specific data[...], citations, and definitions"}}.<ref name="Detecting"/>

;The platform as a subject
{{See also|#Criticisms and current limitations}}
A study showed that when evaluating policies via Kialo debates, "reading comments from most to least liked, on average, displays more [winning arguments] than reading comments earliest first".<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Young |first1=Anthony P. |last2=Joglekar |first2=Sagar |last3=Boschi |first3=Gioia |last4=Sastry |first4=Nishanth |title=Ranking comment sorting policies in online debates |journal=Argument & Computation |date=1 January 2021 |volume=12 |issue=2 |pages=265–285 |doi=10.3233/AAC-200909 |s2cid=228956951 |language=en |issn=1946-2166|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name="Young"/> Kialo has a set of different permissions that participants can have in a given debate. A [[preprint]] study makes suggestions regarding "interface design as a scalable solution to conflict management" to prevent adversarial beliefs and values of moderators to have negative impacts on the site.<ref name="10.31219/osf.io/cdfq7">{{cite journal |title=Managing Conflict in Online Debate Communities: Foregrounding Moderators' Beliefs and Values on Kialo |doi=10.31219/osf.io/cdfq7 |url=https://osf.io/cdfq7/download |last1=Beck |first1=Jordan |last2=Neupane |first2=Bikalpa |last3=Carroll |first3=John M. |s2cid=239864855 |access-date=2023-06-11 |archive-date= |archive-url= |url-status= }}</ref>

== Reception, motivation and distinction from alternatives ==
In 2022, MakeUseOf named the site as one of the five best "debate sites to civilly and logically argue online about opinions"<ref name="makeuseofKialo"/> and in 2019 as one of the "100+ best websites on the Internet".<ref name="muo100">{{cite web |title=The 100+ Best Websites on the Internet |url=https://www.makeuseof.com/tag/best-websites-internet/ |website=MUO |access-date=9 June 2023 |language=en |date=30 November 2019 |archive-date=11 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611174155/https://www.makeuseof.com/tag/best-websites-internet/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

;Online discourse quality
The site aims to be a hub for civilized debate where shouting, rudeness or irrationality aren't allowed.<ref name="fitimes"/><ref name="niemanreports"/> This has been described as remarkable in an "age of [[Twitter use by Donald Trump|Trumpian tweeting]]".<ref name="fitimes"/> The site's founder stated that he noticed early on that the Web became "ideal for bad conversations, with prominence given to the most outrageous conversations" and that he "wondered if there wasn't a better method of online discourse", claiming the site's mission is to "empower reason and to [[Neuroenhancement#Conventional methods and foundational strategies|make the world more thoughtful]]",<ref name="fitimes"/><ref name="about"/><ref>{{cite book |last1=Killenberg |first1=G. Michael |last2=Anderson |first2=Rob |title=Democracy's News: A Primer on Journalism for Citizens Who Care about Democracy |date=20 February 2023 |publisher=University of Michigan Press |isbn=978-0-472-05584-5 |pages=383 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=f86kEAAAQBAJ&pg=PA383 |language=en |access-date=11 June 2023 |archive-date=11 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611175132/https://books.google.com/books?id=f86kEAAAQBAJ&pg=PA383 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="978-1-0718-8702-8"/> describing it as a "platform where people with opposing views can meet and understand each other's thinking".<ref>{{cite web |title=xpmethod {{!}} Group for experimental methods in the humanities |url=https://xpmethod.columbia.edu/events/2016-11-08-kialo.html |website=xpmethod.columbia.edu |access-date=9 June 2023 |archive-date=2023-06-11 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611174159/https://xpmethod.columbia.edu/events/2016-11-08-kialo.html |url-status=live }}</ref> As of 2023, there are major concerns about online irrational or [[Misinformation#Online misinformation|misinformation]]-fueled debate – for example, a researcher affirmed<ref name="irishdebate">{{cite news |title=Kialo offers online debate where nobody shouts |url=https://www.irishtimes.com/business/technology/kialo-offers-online-debate-where-nobody-shouts-1.3375020 |access-date=9 June 2023 |newspaper=The Irish Times |language=en |archive-date=11 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611174155/https://www.irishtimes.com/business/technology/kialo-offers-online-debate-where-nobody-shouts-1.3375020 |url-status=live }}</ref> that "[[Twitter]] was not designed or intended to be a digital town square" as part of a "functioning democracy", addressing Elon Musk's comments about the site in 2022. Instead, she claims it to be a "space for millions of town criers, but not a town square for people to come together and debate".<ref>{{cite news |last1=Maddox |first1=Jessica |title=Elon Musk's comments about Twitter don't square with the social media platform's reality |url=https://techxplore.com/news/2022-05-elon-musk-comments-twitter-dont.html |access-date=25 September 2022 |work=techxplore.com |language=en |archive-date=25 September 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220925223732/https://techxplore.com/news/2022-05-elon-musk-comments-twitter-dont.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Reports suggest the site may present a more complete and complex view of [[reality]] than some other sites where "it's easy to get trapped in [[Echo chamber|echo-chambers]] of like-minded people where your beliefs are never [meaningfully] challenged" as it shows you "the best arguments on both sides of a debate".<ref>{{cite web |last1=Stillman |first1=Jessica |title=10 Websites That Will Give You Superpowers |work=Inc |date=30 January 2023 |url=https://www.inc.com/jessica-stillman/10-websites-that-will-give-you-superpowers.html |publisher=Inc.com |access-date=9 June 2023 |archive-date=11 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611174159/https://www.inc.com/jessica-stillman/10-websites-that-will-give-you-superpowers.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="harvardexample">{{cite web |title=Debating Solar Geoengineering on the Kialo Visual Reasoning Platform |url=https://geoengineering.environment.harvard.edu/blog/debating-solar-geoengineering-kialo-visual-reasoning-platform |website=geoengineering.environment.harvard.edu |access-date=9 June 2023 |language=en |date=25 September 2018 |archive-date=11 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611174208/https://geoengineering.environment.harvard.edu/blog/debating-solar-geoengineering-kialo-visual-reasoning-platform |url-status=live }}</ref>

;Communication formats
{{tooltip|Standard digital formats|such as a discussion board, Twitter feed or comment thread}} e.g. "tend to only allow a linear progression of arguments in a stream-of-discussion format".<ref name="structured"/> On many websites, "circuitous comment threads [often] render meaningful discussion impossible" and "formats that we use to communicate [[Social shaping of technology|shape]] the way we communicate".<ref name="chonicEd">{{cite news |title=How to Promote Enlightened Debate Online |url=https://www.chronicle.com/article/how-to-promote-enlightened-debate-online/ |access-date=9 June 2023 |work=[[The Chronicle of Higher Education]] |date=25 March 2018 |first1=Audrey Williams |last1=June |language=en |archive-date=11 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611174154/https://www.chronicle.com/article/how-to-promote-enlightened-debate-online/ |url-status=live }}</ref> On the site, users contribute to a debate tree rather than engaging in argumentative back-and-forth commenting.<ref>{{cite web |title=Debate as pedagogy: Practices, tools, and examples from Harvard faculty – Harvard Initiative for Learning and Teaching (HILT) |url=https://hilt.harvard.edu/news-and-events/events/debate-as-pedagogy-practices-tools-and-examples-from-harvard-faculty/ |website=hilt.harvard.edu |access-date=16 July 2023 |quote=Kialo, where students make “claims” about a thesis, contributing to a visual debate tree that empowers reason rather than argumentative commenting |archive-date=29 May 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230529030452/https://hilt.harvard.edu/news-and-events/events/debate-as-pedagogy-practices-tools-and-examples-from-harvard-faculty/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Kialo may be more appropriate especially for discussions that are relatively complex and hard to visualize or oversee otherwise and allows for public ideation and structured interaction among different types of stakeholders.<ref name="harvardexample"/> Linking to supporting evidence is encouraged,<ref name="irishdebate"/> but not as strictly required as for example on Wikipedia. Kialo has advantages over structured knowledge bases and Wikipedia in "that it includes many debatable statements; many attacked sentences are subjective judgments, so fact-based knowledge sources may have limited utility".<ref name="Detecting"/> Chains of reasoning can be followed "from beginning to end" with relatively little text to read, nearly no repetition or unexplained statements and without having it derailed by for example "name-calling and directionless ranting".<ref name="irishdebate"/> Online debates "have grown so large and acrimonious that no one realistically has the time to read everything and hence get a sense of the actually winning arguments (winners) after all points have been considered" and there is research into how to efficiently calculate the winning arguments or arguments weights and the overall conclusions.<ref name="Young">{{cite web |last1=Young |first1=Anthony P. |title=Likes as Argument Strength for Online Debate |url=https://argstrength2021.argumentationcompetition.org/papers/ArgStrength2021_paper_8.pdf |access-date=10 June 2023 |archive-date=11 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611174159/https://argstrength2021.argumentationcompetition.org/papers/ArgStrength2021_paper_8.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref> Moreover, argumentations on the site are less fleeting and repetitive than debates on social media sites – they are commonly read and actively contributed to over the span of years.<ref name="techlearning"/><ref name="chonicEd"/>

;Criticisms and current limitations
{{More citations needed section|date=July 2023}}
One [[preprint]] study stated that "[t]hough kialo is designed for scale, and therefore has to be not only robust but also both easy and appealing to use, it has simplified its notion of argument structure so much that there is very little flexibility left. As a commercial entity, its data [not reusable] and platform [not [[free and open source software|open source]]] are also closed, making wide-scale application at the science-policy [[Evidence-based policy#Scholarly communication in policy|interface]] more challenging."<ref>{{cite arXiv |title=Managing Expert Disagreement for the Policy Process and Beyond |eprint=2212.14714 |last1=Hahn |first1=Ulrike |author2=Jens Koed Madsen |last3=Reed |first3=Chris |year=2022 |class=cs.CY }}</ref>

One study found that "Kialo's simplicity does pose some weaknesses and limitations" and found the functionality of current systems including Kialo for "synthesis of arguments" to be insufficient.<ref name="Complexity"/> One study suggests the platform is structured in a way that gives insufficient capacity for users to do anything else other than to either agree or disagree with a side,<ref>{{cite book |last1=Althuniyan |first1=Najla |last2=Sirrianni |first2=Joseph W. |last3=Rahman |first3=Md Mahfuzer |last4=Liu |first4=Xiaoqing "Frank" |chapter=Design of Mobile Service of Intelligent Large-Scale Cyber Argumentation for Analysis and Prediction of Collective Opinions |title=Artificial Intelligence and Mobile Services – AIMS 2019 |series=Lecture Notes in Computer Science |date=2019 |volume=11516 |pages=135–149 |doi=10.1007/978-3-030-23367-9_10 |publisher=Springer International Publishing |isbn=978-3-030-23366-2 |s2cid=195353310 |language=en}}</ref> with there e.g. only being options to rate the veracity of the main thesis but not for proposing concrete alternatives and middle-grounds such as more nuanced policies or specifying conditional critical considerations (e.g. exceptions, applicable scopes and limitations) of one's veracity rating of the main thesis, which tend to be very brief and rarely revised.

One study points out that without 'Writer' permissions in a debate, the arguments have "to get past the gatekeepers" of it, which can in some cases be problematic as moderators' beliefs and values may play a role.<ref name="10.31219/osf.io/cdfq7"/> For instance, such can lead to some users feeling like certain perspectives (or arguments) are being excluded from a debate<ref name="10.31219/osf.io/cdfq7"/> or getting positioned inappropriately (such as not being visible at the level most relevant). There may be issues relating to framing and argument positioning, whereby for example a false claim (with or without a source) can be added as supporting a thesis which is then only addressed by a later countering claim stating the opposite beneath it – which may reduce the former's 'Impact' rating but is not shown directly at the tree level above as an 'countering' argument. Instead, only the false or weak supporting argument can be seen at the level above in such a case. Impact rating votes do not require reading the arguments beneath but voting can be turned off until the argument map has had time to sufficiently develop.<ref>{{cite web |title=Using Voting {{!}} Kialo Help Center |url=https://support.kialo.com/en/hc/using-voting/ |website=support.kialo.com |date=6 April 2023 |access-date=18 July 2023 |archive-date=4 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230604170229/https://support.kialo.com/en/hc/using-voting/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

;Complementarity
The founder clarified key distinctions and complementarity of the site saying "We're going to just be an added place. We're not competing with anybody out there with regards to thoughtful discourse. There are a couple of sites that are [[Comparison of Q&A sites|question-and-answer sites]], or commenting sites, or sharing sites, but there's not a single [major] site for collaborative reasoning — a repository of the [[Reason (argument)|why]]".<ref name="chonicEd"/> He states that Wikipedia – another [[peer production]] site to which Kialo is sometimes compared with due to argumentative discussions on [[Talk pages]]<ref name="guo"/> and its public collaborative knowledge integration<ref name="10.31219/osf.io/cdfq7"/><ref name="Dialectics"/> – "tells you the what and we tell you the why".<ref name="chonicEd"/>
